title: The four pillars of OOP
idea: Object-oriented programming builds a program from objects that pair data with the behaviour that guards it, shaped by four ideas: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance and polymorphism.
points: Encapsulation keeps fields `private` and lets only methods change them.
Abstraction exposes a contract, an `interface`, and hides how it works.
Inheritance lets a subclass reuse a parent through an is-a link.
Polymorphism picks the method to run from the object's real class.

code.title: Abstraction and polymorphism
code.caption: Three fee rules behind one interface. The loop never asks which class it holds.

walk.text: `Fee` is the contract: one method to compute, one default method for a name.
A `record` implements the interface: a small immutable value with behaviour.
`PercentFee` keeps its rate `private final`: set once, never changed.
`CappedFee` extends `PercentFee` via `super`; whether it truly is-a percent fee is a Liskov question for later.
The override reuses the parent's result with `super.on`, then applies the cap.
The list holds `Fee`; each `fee.on` call runs the real class's method.

code.title: Encapsulation
code.caption: The balance can change only through `pay`, which refuses bad amounts.

walk.text: The field is `private` with no setter, so no caller can write it.
The constructor rejects a bad opening value: objects start valid.
`pay` rejects a bad argument, then a bad state, before it changes anything.
The caller sees the refusal as an exception; the balance is untouched.

pitfalls: Do not extend a class only to reuse code; without a true is-a, use composition.
Avoid public fields and blind setters; they let any caller break your rules.
Add `@Override` to every override, so a typo or overload fails to compile.

quiz.why: Dynamic dispatch uses the runtime class. `getClass()` names `CappedFee`, and its override caps the parent's 40 at 30.
quiz.code:
Fee fee = new CappedFee(2, 30);
System.out.println(fee.name() + " on 2000 = " + fee.on(2000));

takeaway: Hide state, code to contracts, inherit only for is-a, let dispatch choose.
